body.x: Gbrain (Co-CEOs Byoung Kim and Sunggu Yang) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Gbrain has focused on treatment gaps and unmet medical needs that conventional deep-brain stimulation (DBS) cannot address, and has developed electrical stimulation therapy technology based on cortical electrodes. Founded in 2019 with the goal of commercializing medical devices that move beyond laboratory-level technology to actual patient treatment, the company has pursued full-scale business development.

Since its establishment, Gbrain has built the entire value chain of research and development, manufacturing, quality control, and clinical operations step by step, centered on fully implantable brain nerve stimulation technology. After completing an ISO Class 7 cleanroom-based manufacturing facility in 2022 to secure infrastructure for implantable medical device production, the company established a GMP-compliant production system in 2024 and obtained certification.

Furthermore, through national R&D projects, Gbrain advanced the development of fully implantable closed-loop brain nerve stimulation technology, verifying technological sophistication and clinical applicability, and it has attracted cumulative investment totaling approximately 8 billion won to date.

At CES 2026, Gbrain unveiled “Phin Stim,” a product that represents its accumulated R&D capabilities. Phin Stim is a fully implantable brain nerve stimulator that integrates ultra-thin, highly flexible cortical electrodes with circuitry. Using its proprietary electrode technology, the device closely adheres to the cortical surface to stably acquire high-resolution brain signals. The collected brain signals go beyond simple recording and are processed immediately within the device for therapeutic decision-making.

The circuitry of Phin Stim employs AI-based signal processing. This technology analyzes brain waves in real time to assess the patient’s current neural state and automatically adjusts stimulation intensity and patterns accordingly. Unlike conventional methods that repeat pre-set stimulation, Phin Stim implements a closed-loop, dynamically responsive stimulation that adapts to changes in brain state.

In addition, Phin Stim is designed to enable brain signal-based stimulation control and functional expansion through brain-computer interface (BCI) technology. This allows not only precise stimulation optimization according to patient condition but also future expansion into various neurological indications beyond Parkinson’s disease, including stroke rehabilitation and paralysis.

A Gbrain official said, “Phin Stim is a core product that embodies our technological differentiation and mid- to long-term growth strategy, and through it we sought to propose fully implantable brain nerve stimulation technology and a BCI-based approach to the global market.” The official added, “As we created meaningful opportunities by meeting various stakeholders, including global medical device companies, hospitals, and research institutions at CES, we plan to accelerate overseas partnerships and commercialization through continued technical and clinical discussions.”

The official continued, “Gbrain is currently establishing a systematic U.S. regulatory approval strategy with the goal of submitting to the FDA within this year, and we expect strong commercialization potential in North America, where demand for innovative medical devices is high and clinical infrastructure is well developed.” The official added, “While accumulating clinical evidence and responding to regulatory requirements in parallel, we will focus on securing global partnerships and pursuing phased business expansion.”

body.x: The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
